title: A Fall Can Carry a Signal

scenes.visual: Dark slate (#0F172A) frame. A cross-section of a rod outer segment fills 70% of the frame height: disc membrane on the left holding rhodopsin, plasma membrane on the right with open cation channels. Teal (#2DD4BF) cGMP dots drift through the cytosol while sky-blue (#38BDF8) ions flow steadily inward. Crisp off-white title 'A Fall Can Carry a Signal' (size 40) fades in, holds briefly, and fades out by 2.0 s.

scenes.tts: A rod cell detects a single photon by turning an electrical current down. How can destroying a messenger carry a signal? Every cascade you met before made a messenger appear. Start with a rod resting in darkness.
scenes.caption: A rod cell detects a single photon by turning an electrical current down. How can destroying a messenger carry a signal? Every cascade you met before made a messenger appear. Start with a rod resting in darkness.
scenes.visual: Keep the rod cross-section in place. A live schematic current trace in sky blue (#38BDF8, labelled 'schematic') sweeps steadily at a high baseline across the bottom. A single gold (#FACC15) photon arrow briefly flashes onto the left disc and causes a sharp downward dip on the trace, then resets smoothly to darkness as the label 'Dark state' appears (size 28, off-white).
scenes.narration: A rod cell detects a single photon by turning an electrical current down. How can destroying a messenger carry a signal? Every cascade you met before made a messenger appear. Start with a rod resting in darkness.

scenes.tts: In darkness, guanylyl cyclase keeps making c G M P, while its breakdown runs only slowly. So c G M P stays high. This messenger binds directly to cation channels, holding some of them open with no kinase in between. Sodium and calcium stream inward. That steady dark current leaves the rod partly depolarized, releasing glutamate nonstop.
scenes.caption: In darkness, guanylyl cyclase keeps making cGMP, while its breakdown runs only slowly. So cGMP stays high. This messenger binds directly to cation channels, holding some of them open with no kinase in between. Sodium and calcium stream inward. That steady dark current leaves the rod partly depolarized, releasing glutamate nonstop.
scenes.visual: Emerald-green (#34D399) guanylyl cyclase pulses steadily, replenishing teal (#2DD4BF) cGMP dots while rose (#F43F5E) PDE6 idles slowly. Teal cGMP dots dock directly onto some of the right-hand cation channels, holding those gates open while the others stay shut. Sky-blue (#38BDF8) sodium and coral-orange (#FB923C) calcium beads stream inward; at the bottom right, steady bursts of glutamate dots exit the synapse. A teal gauge on the far left holds high. Empathy fix: Show 'Make (cyclase): steady' beside 'Break (PDE6, idling): slow' as the first sentence is spoken.
scenes.narration: In darkness, guanylyl cyclase keeps making cGMP, while its breakdown runs only slowly. So cGMP stays high. This messenger binds directly to cation channels, holding some of them open with no kinase in between. Sodium and calcium stream inward. That steady dark current leaves the rod partly depolarized, releasing glutamate nonstop.

scenes.tts: Inside the disc membrane sits rhodopsin, a receptor holding bent retinal already inside its pocket. That bent shape locks rhodopsin off. When a photon arrives, it straightens retinal, and the protein around it is pushed into a new shape. Rhodopsin is now active, and every later step runs without light.
scenes.caption: Inside the disc membrane sits rhodopsin, a receptor holding bent retinal already inside its pocket. That bent shape locks rhodopsin off. When a photon arrives, it straightens retinal, and the protein around it is pushed into a new shape. Rhodopsin is now active, and every later step runs without light.
scenes.visual: Smoothly enlarge the rhodopsin cartoon on the left disc membrane while keeping the rest of the rod faintly visible for continuity. Inside its pocket sits a bent schematic bar labelled '11-cis retinal' (no chemical structure). A gold (#FACC15) photon wave strikes it; the bar straightens cleanly into 'all-trans retinal', pushing the rhodopsin block into a glowing gold active shape.
scenes.narration: Inside the disc membrane sits rhodopsin, a receptor holding bent retinal already inside its pocket. That bent shape locks rhodopsin off. When a photon arrives, it straightens retinal, and the protein around it is pushed into a new shape. Rhodopsin is now active, and every later step runs without light.

scenes.tts: Active rhodopsin switches on many copies of transducin, swapping G D P for G T P. Activated transducin lifts an inhibitory cap off the phosphodiesterase P D E six. The freed enzyme rapidly breaks c G M P into inactive G M P. As messenger levels plunge, channels snap shut.
scenes.caption: Active rhodopsin switches on many copies of transducin, swapping GDP for GTP. Activated transducin lifts an inhibitory cap off the phosphodiesterase PDE6. The freed enzyme rapidly breaks cGMP into inactive GMP. As messenger levels plunge, channels snap shut.
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the full carried rod cross-section. Gold active rhodopsin contacts a stream of transducin blocks whose tags flip from GDP to gold GTP. Transducin-GTP docks onto rose (#F43F5E) PDE6 and slides off its grey inhibitory lid. PDE6 spins rapidly, converting teal (#2DD4BF) cGMP dots into fading grey GMP dots. The teal cGMP gauge plunges, teal dots unbind the right-hand channels, and the gates snap shut.
scenes.narration: Active rhodopsin switches on many copies of transducin, swapping GDP for GTP. Activated transducin lifts an inhibitory cap off the phosphodiesterase PDE6. The freed enzyme rapidly breaks cGMP into inactive GMP. As messenger levels plunge, channels snap shut.

scenes.tts: With channels closed, positive inflow shrinks, the membrane hyperpolarizes, and glutamate release drops. The next neuron reads that drop as light. To reset, phosphorylation and arrestin silence rhodopsin, while G T P hydrolysis turns transducin off. Still, the rod must refill its depleted messenger pool.
scenes.caption: With channels closed, positive inflow shrinks, the membrane hyperpolarizes, and glutamate release drops. The next neuron reads that drop as light. To reset, phosphorylation and arrestin silence rhodopsin, while GTP hydrolysis turns transducin off. Still, the rod must refill its depleted messenger pool.
scenes.visual: On the same rod, the sky-blue (#38BDF8) ion stream stops, the bottom schematic current trace dips sharply, and glutamate dots at the synapse dwindle. Next, small phosphate tags and an arrestin cap quiet gold rhodopsin back to dim slate; transducin-GTP reverts to GDP and the lid clamps back onto rose PDE6. The teal cGMP gauge remains low.
scenes.narration: With channels closed, positive inflow shrinks, the membrane hyperpolarizes, and glutamate release drops. The next neuron reads that drop as light. To reset, phosphorylation and arrestin silence rhodopsin, while GTP hydrolysis turns transducin off. Still, the rod must refill its depleted messenger pool.

scenes.tts: While channels stood open in darkness, calcium entered steadily and an exchanger pumped it back out. Light closed the channels, so entry stopped, pumping continued, and calcium fell. Low calcium switches on helper proteins that speed up guanylyl cyclase. Now keep a dim light shining. Will the channels stay shut?
scenes.caption: While channels stood open in darkness, calcium entered steadily and an exchanger pumped it back out. Light closed the channels, so entry stopped, pumping continued, and calcium fell. Low calcium switches on helper proteins that speed up guanylyl cyclase. Now keep a dim light shining. Will the channels stay shut?
scenes.visual: Highlight coral-orange (#FB923C) calcium dots inside the rod: closed channels stop entry while a pumping arrow at the membrane keeps pushing coral-orange calcium out, and a coral-orange 'Ca2+' gauge drops smoothly. Small helper blocks labelled 'GCAPs' dock onto emerald-green (#34D399) guanylyl cyclase, which brightens. A faint steady gold (#FACC15) wash of background light settles over the left discs. A crisp off-white question card appears: 'Steady light: do the channels stay shut?'
scenes.narration: While channels stood open in darkness, calcium entered steadily and an exchanger pumped it back out. Light closed the channels, so entry stopped, pumping continued, and calcium fell. Low calcium switches on helper proteins that speed up guanylyl cyclase. Now keep a dim light shining. Will the channels stay shut?

scenes.visual: Hold the question card 'Steady light: do the channels stay shut?' clearly visible for 4.5 seconds. The faint gold background-light wash stays on, the low Ca2+ gauge holds still, and a subtle pulsing question mark hovers over the closed channels so the frame stays alive without giving away the answer.

scenes.tts: No. The faster cyclase refills the messenger partway, so some channels reopen under the light. This negative feedback lets the rod adapt to background light. With some channels open again, the rod has current left to shut off, so an extra flash still registers.
scenes.caption: No. The faster cyclase refills the messenger partway, so some channels reopen under the light. This negative feedback lets the rod adapt to background light. With some channels open again, the rod has current left to shut off, so an extra flash still registers.
scenes.visual: The question card fades out while the faint gold background-light wash stays on. Brightened emerald-green (#34D399) guanylyl cyclase streams fresh teal (#2DD4BF) cGMP dots into the cytosol; a coral-orange feedback arrow links the low Ca2+ gauge to the cyclase. The teal gauge climbs partway back up, a few channels reopen, and the bottom schematic trace rebounds to a mid-level baseline ready to dip again for an extra gold flash. Empathy fix: Label the partly recovered trace 'Current left to shut off', then show it dip again at the extra flash.
scenes.narration: No. The faster cyclase refills the messenger partway, so some channels reopen under the light. This negative feedback lets the rod adapt to background light. With some channels open again, the rod has current left to shut off, so an extra flash still registers.

scenes.tts: Now compare the eye with the nose. Each olfactory neuron expresses a single odorant receptor from a very large family. When an odorant binds, a G protein activates adenylyl cyclase, so c A M P rises. The rising messenger opens a related cation channel, and the neuron depolarizes and fires.
scenes.caption: Now compare the eye with the nose. Each olfactory neuron expresses a single odorant receptor from a very large family. When an odorant binds, a G protein activates adenylyl cyclase, so cAMP rises. The rising messenger opens a related cation channel, and the neuron depolarizes and fires.
scenes.visual: Slide the rod smoothly to the left half of the frame and build a matching olfactory sensory neuron cross-section on the right half. An odorant dot binds a single receptor, activating a G protein and emerald-green (#34D399) adenylyl cyclase. Warm-amber (#F59E0B) cAMP dots rise on a matching amber gauge and open a cation channel; sky-blue (#38BDF8) ions rush inward as the neuron membrane glows active.
scenes.narration: Now compare the eye with the nose. Each olfactory neuron expresses a single odorant receptor from a very large family. When an odorant binds, a G protein activates adenylyl cyclase, so cAMP rises. The rising messenger opens a related cation channel, and the neuron depolarizes and fires.

scenes.tts: Both senses rely on closely related cyclic-nucleotide channels, yet wire them in opposite directions. Light drives c G M P down from its dark baseline. An odorant drives the nose's messenger up from rest. Keep this rule. A signal is a change from baseline, up or down.
scenes.caption: Both senses rely on closely related cyclic-nucleotide channels, yet wire them in opposite directions. Light drives cGMP down from its dark baseline. An odorant drives the nose's messenger up from rest. Keep this rule. A signal is a change from baseline, up or down.
scenes.visual: Keep the side-by-side gauges prominent and filling 65% of the frame: on the left, 'Rod: cGMP falls' with a teal (#2DD4BF) arrow dropping below a dashed baseline; on the right, 'Nose: cAMP rises' with a warm-amber (#F59E0B) arrow climbing above its dashed baseline. Both gauges gently pulse around their baselines.
